_comment: Every registry write is lock, re-read, change, save - Registry.mutate, directly or through tracking. The CLI's flash add-prompt, add-mcu's adoption and add-type each wrote a registry they had read before a prompt, with no lock: an edit the panel made while the prompt waited was erased by the save, and the prompt and adoption writes skipped tracking's refusals, so a board could end up tracked under two types or an unprovisioned Roadrunner's flash UID could be persisted. add_type refuses a name another builder declares, whatever overwrite says: the CLI passes overwrite=True with a kconfig-only pre-check, and _save would rewrite the other builder's section as a kconfig type with its serials emptied. Settings live in the same file and go through settings.mutate the same way - lock, then load, change, write: without the lock an agent settings write racing a CLI add-serial loses one of the two edits, and with a load taken before the lock a fw.bus.ignore that finished while fw.settings.set waited is written back out of the ignore list.

mutations.name: the flash add-prompt tracks through tracking, not an unlocked direct write
add-mcu adoption tracks through tracking, so a board tracked elsewhere is refused

with Registry.mutate(c.paths, "adopt") as writable:

except UpdaterError as exc:
                print(f"ERROR: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)

mutations.name: add-type writes under the registry lock
mutations.find:
with Registry.mutate(c.paths, f"add type {args.type}") as writable:
        writable.add_type(
            args.type,
            args.chipset,
            klipper_args=args.klipper_args,
            katapult_args=args.katapult_args,
            katapult_installed=not args.no_katapult,
            overwrite=True,
        )
mutations.replace:
if True:

        writable.add_type(

            klipper_args=args.klipper_args,
            katapult_args=args.katapult_args,
            katapult_installed=not args.no_katapult,
            overwrite=True,
        )
        writable._save(c.paths)
